votes.motion: Approve the April 1, 2025, and May 20, 2025 work session meeting minutes.
votes.description: Approval of two prior work session meeting minutes from April 1, 2025 and May 20, 2025.

votes.motion: Adopt the Joint Ceremonial Resolution 27 of 2025, recognizing September as National Suicide Prevention Month in Salt Lake City.
votes.description: A joint ceremonial resolution with Mayor Mendenhall declaring September as National Suicide Prevention Month in Salt Lake City, highlighting resources such as the 988 mental health hotline.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer Items B1 – B6 to a future Consent Agenda for action.
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on six grant applications (Regional Athletic Complex, Civic Center District/Green Loop, Jordan River Trail, COPS De-Escalation Training, River & Roots, and Juvenile Fire Setter Prevention) and refers them to a future consent agenda for action.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer action to a future council meeting (Zoning Map Amendment at Approximately 247 North 800 West).
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on a proposed rezone of properties at approximately 247 North 800 West from R-1/7,000 and SR-3 to R-1/5,000 and SR-3, and defers action to a future council meeting.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer to a future council meeting for action (Alley Vacation at Approximately 373 West American Avenue).
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on a proposed ordinance to vacate a City-owned alley adjacent to properties at approximately 373 West American Avenue, and defers action to a future council meeting.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and defer action to a future council meeting (Zoning Text Amendment Public Lands and Street Vacation – West High School).
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on proposed zoning text amendments to the Public Lands district and a street vacation related to the reconstruction of West High School at approximately 240 West 200 North, and defers action to a future council meeting.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and defer action to a future council meeting for action (Zoning Map Amendment for the Delta Center Parking Garage at Approximately 301 West South Temple).
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on a proposed Master Development Agreement for a seven-story parking garage at the Delta Center Arena at approximately 301 West South Temple, and defers action to a future council meeting.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 28 of 2025, Public Utilities Bond Anticipation Notes, Series 2025B and Revenue Refunding Bonds, Series 2025C parameters, and refer to the consent agenda for setting the date for a public hearing on the bond issuance for October 7, 2025.
votes.description: Authorizes the issuance and sale of up to $50,000,000 in Public Utilities revenue bond anticipation notes (Series 2025B) to finance a Public Utilities campus, and up to $50,000,000 in revenue refunding bonds (Series 2025C) to refund outstanding Series 2017 bonds, and sets a public hearing date.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 29 of 2025, Building Permit Fee Waivers for Alliance House and First Step House.
votes.description: Approves building permit fee waivers for two non-profit developers—Alliance House (16 units at approximately 1805 South Main Street) and First Step House (67 units at approximately 44 North 1000 West)—for deeply affordable housing projects serving households at or below 30–40% AMI.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 53 of 2025, amending the annual compensation plan for all non-represented employees for the fiscal year 2025-26.
votes.description: Amends the FY 2025-26 Annual Compensation Plan for non-represented employees to include policy updates for operational efficiency and employee retention, as well as corrections related to City retirement contributions.

Approves all consent agenda items including setting public hearing dates, approving Grant Holding Account items, and approving board appointments and reappointments to the Public Utilities Advisory Committee, Planning Commission, and Historic Landmark Commission.
